title: Frobenius substitution and geometric Frobenius of a finite field
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a finite field with $q$ elements [def-weil-finite-field-q-elements] and let $k$ be an algebraic closure of $k_0$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; write $\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ for the group of field automorphisms of $k$ that fix $k_0$ pointwise. The *Frobenius substitution* (arithmetic Frobenius) is the map

$$
 \varphi_q:k\longrightarrow k,\qquad z\longmapsto z^q ;
$$

it is a field automorphism of $k$ fixing $k_0$ pointwise (additive because $q$ is a power of the characteristic $p$, fixing $k_0$ because $c^q=c$ for $c\in k_0$, injective as a field homomorphism, surjective because every element of $k$ lies in a finite subfield on which it is an injective self-map), so $\varphi_q\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$. The *geometric Frobenius* is its inverse

$$
 \operatorname{Frob}_q=\varphi_q^{-1}\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0).
$$

source.place: (1.1.7), p. 150 (pdf p. 15): 'La substitution de Frobenius φ ∈ Gal(k̄/k) est l'automorphisme x ↦ x^q de k̄. Le Frobenius géométrique F ∈ Gal(k̄/k) est l'inverse de φ.'
